name: atproto-datepair-v2
instr:
**Labeler declaration republished from Python says we accept no reports**

We publish our community labeler's `app.bsky.labeler.service` declaration from a Python script:
an `AppBskyLabelerService.Record` with our label values and definitions in `policies`. Reason
types and subject types stay unset on purpose: per the lexicon, not defined (as opposed to an
empty array) means every kind of report is accepted. Subject collections is an empty list, since
we only take reports about accounts, not individual posts.

After upgrading atproto we re-ran the script to add a label, and reports stopped arriving. curl
on our PDS's `com.atproto.repo.getRecord` shows `"reasonTypes": []` and `"subjectTypes": []`,
i.e. nothing can be reported. We never set those. Our nightly backup, which pulls the whole repo
from the PDS and loads it with the SDK, had reason types and subject types unset last night.

The checkout is in /workdir. Could you track down where this actually goes wrong and fix it
there? Please include a regression test, somewhere under tests/ (say tests/test_repro.py), that fails on the current code because
of this problem (a real test failure, not an import error) and passes once it's fixed.
Test the reported behaviour, not your patch: it should still pass if the bug gets fixed some other correct
way, so no asserting on source text or on helpers only your fix has. It should run on its own
from a clean checkout with just your test files added.

I doubt I'm the only one hitting this
